recipes.name: Masoor Dal & Palak Curry (Dairy-Free)
recipes.health_benefit: Rich in soluble fiber from lentils and spinach, which may help lower LDL cholesterol. Provides plant-based protein and iron, essential for overall health.

ingredients.item: Rice Bran Oil or Mustard Oil

instructions: Wash masoor dal thoroughly and soak for 20-30 minutes. Drain.
Heat oil in a pressure cooker or heavy-bottomed pan. Add mustard seeds and cumin seeds; let them splutter. Add asafoetida.
Add chopped onion and sauté until golden brown. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili, cook for 1-2 minutes until aromatic.
Add tomato puree and cook until the oil separates.
Stir in turmeric powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the drained dal and chopped spinach. Mix well.

Add 3-4 cups of water and salt to taste. If using a pressure cooker, close the lid and cook for 2-3 whistles. If using a pan, cover and simmer until dal is tender (approx. 20-25 minutes), adding more water if needed.
Once cooked, mash lightly with the back of a spoon if desired. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
Serve hot with brown rice or whole wheat roti.

recipes.name: Tandoori Fish Tikka (Dairy-Free)
recipes.health_benefit: Fatty fish like salmon or mackerel are excellent sources of Omega-3 fatty acids, which can help manage triglyceride levels and support heart health. This recipe is lean and flavorful without dairy.

ingredients.item: Rice Bran Oil or Mustard Oil

instructions: Pat fish pieces dry. In a bowl, combine lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala, black pepper, and salt. Mix well to form a thick paste.
Add fish pieces to the marinade, ensuring they are well coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F) or prepare a grill/grill pan.
Thread the marinated fish pieces onto skewers, alternating with onion and bell pepper squares if using.
Brush the fish and vegetables lightly with oil.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, flipping halfway, or grill until cooked through and slightly charred. Cooking time will vary based on fish thickness.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with mint chutney.

recipes.name: Vegetable Oats Upma (Dairy-Free)
recipes.health_benefit: Oats are a great source of soluble fiber (beta-glucan) which is known to help reduce LDL cholesterol. This dish provides sustained energy and is packed with vegetables for vitamins and minerals.
instructions: Dry roast oats in a pan for 3-4 minutes until lightly fragrant. Set aside.
Heat oil in the same pan. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and curry leaves. Let them splutter.
Add peanuts and sauté until lightly roasted. Remove half for garnish.
Add chopped onion, green chili, and grated ginger. Sauté until onion turns translucent.
Add mixed vegetables and cook for 3-5 minutes until slightly tender.
Add water and salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, slowly add the roasted oats, stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Cover and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until all water is absorbed and oats are cooked.
Turn off heat, stir in lemon juice. Garnish with fresh coriander and remaining roasted peanuts.
Serve hot.

recipes.name: Sprouted Moong Dal Salad
recipes.health_benefit: Sprouted moong dal is rich in fiber and plant protein, aiding in satiety and digestive health. It's a low-calorie, nutrient-dense snack that contributes to overall well-being and blood sugar balance.
instructions: If moong dal is not already sprouted, soak whole moong dal overnight, then drain and keep in a moist cloth in a warm place for 1-2 days until sprouts appear.
In a mixing bowl, combine sprouted moong dal, chopped cucumber, tomato, onion (if using), green chili (if using), and coriander leaves.
Add lemon juice, chaat masala, and black salt.
Toss everything gently until well combined.
Serve immediately as a refreshing and nutritious snack or light meal.

recipes.name: Chicken and Vegetable Stir-fry
recipes.health_benefit: Provides lean protein from chicken and a wide array of vitamins, minerals, and fiber from various vegetables. This low-carb, high-protein meal supports satiety and overall metabolic health without excess saturated fat.

ingredients.quantity: to taste (use sparingly due to soy sauce)

instructions: Heat rice bran oil in a large wok or pan over high heat.
Add chicken strips and stir-fry until cooked through and lightly browned (about 5-7 minutes). Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger to the pan, stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add broccoli and carrots, stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Add bell peppers and mushrooms, stir-fry for another 2-3 minutes.
Return the cooked chicken to the pan.
Pour in low sodium soy sauce, sesame oil (if using), black pepper, and salt (if needed). Toss everything to coat evenly.
Cook for 1-2 more minutes until heated through and flavors are well combined.
Garnish with spring onion greens and serve hot.

recipes.name: Almond & Sesame Ladoo (Dairy-Free)
recipes.health_benefit: These ladoos offer healthy fats from almonds and sesame seeds, which are also excellent non-dairy sources of calcium, crucial for bone health especially with a dairy allergy. Dates provide natural sweetness and fiber.
instructions: Lightly dry roast almonds in a pan for 3-4 minutes until fragrant. Let cool.
Lightly dry roast sesame seeds in a separate pan for 2-3 minutes until they start to pop and turn light golden. Be careful not to burn. Let cool.
In a food processor, combine roasted almonds, roasted sesame seeds, pitted dates, and cardamom powder.
Process until the mixture comes together and forms a sticky dough. If it's too dry, add 1-2 tablespoons of water or a tiny bit of date syrup to help it bind.
Take small portions of the mixture and roll them into firm ladoos (balls).
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to a week or refrigerate for longer. Enjoy one as a healthy snack.
Note: Nutrition is per ladoo (approximately 25-30g each).

lifestyle_advice: **Prioritize Physical Activity:** Maintain your moderately active lifestyle. Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise or 75 minutes of vigorous-intensity exercise per week, combined with muscle-strengthening activities on 2 or more days. This can significantly help manage LDL cholesterol and overall cardiovascular health.
**Manage Stress:** Incorporate stress-reduction techniques such as meditation, deep breathing exercises, yoga, or spending time in nature. Chronic stress can negatively impact metabolic markers.

**Ensure Adequate Sleep:** Aim for 7-9 hours of quality sleep per night. Poor sleep can affect hormone regulation, appetite, and metabolic health, potentially influencing LDL levels and overall well-being.
**Hydration:** Drink plenty of water throughout the day. Proper hydration is essential for all bodily functions, including metabolism and digestion.

**Sun Exposure (for Vitamin D):** While supplementing, consider safe sun exposure (10-15 minutes, 2-3 times per week, exposing arms and legs without sunscreen during non-peak hours) to naturally support Vitamin D production, being mindful of skin protection.
**Regular Check-ups:** Continue regular monitoring of your lipid profile and Vitamin D levels with your healthcare provider to track progress and adjust your plan as needed.
